note: EVAL-5's security corpus (ADR-0048). Every record declares each of the four readers readable or forbidden, and the loader refuses a file where a pair is left out — an undeclared pair is an unmeasured boundary that would still report zero leaks. The tiers and the placements are governed into place, never seeded: `vault-ceremony` reaches `restricted` through a classification proposal its own author opened and two distinct approvers signed, one of them compliance, because that is the only mechanism in the product that mints the tier; `bridge-rota` reaches the vault team's published channel through a real proposal and a real approval, because observe lands records at the caller's home leaf and nothing else can put material above one. The three `forge-*` records are the prompt-injection half: their content carries the block's own structural vocabulary, and the assertion is the same for every record in this file — every non-empty line of a composed block is the preamble, the data notice, a section header, the index legend, the watermark or an entry, and the entries number exactly as many as the watermark names.

material.note: The handle carries a UUID with hex letters in every group, and that is not cosmetic: the first run used an all-zero UUID and MEM-2's `payment-card` rule ate it — `\b(?:\d[ \-]?){12,18}\d\b` matches the digit-and-hyphen run and all zeros passes Luhn — so the record reached the block as `(recall [REDACTED:payment-card]` and this probe was testing the redactor rather than the renderer. The half the fold does NOT close, and the reason security_marker_echoes is reported rather than gated (ADR-0048 decision 11): neutralising this would mean editing the text a memory product exists to return, and the fix that would make it impossible — moving every marker to a prefix position content cannot occupy — is CTX-2/CTX-4's format decision and not an eval's to drive.
